# About this document

This file does two jobs:

1.  **Verification script.** It re-runs every check made on the AI-built master dataset, applies the corrections that came out of those checks, and writes the final files. Run it top to bottom, or press **Render**.
2.  **AI log.** It records what I asked the AI (Claude), what I gave it, what it answered, and what I decided. Repeated attempts are condensed to the version that worked, but the AI's mistakes are kept (see the table at the end), because the log has to show where the AI was wrong as well as right.

**How to read the log entries**

> **Me:** what I wrote to the AI (lightly trimmed for length).
>
> **Claude:** a summary of the AI's answer.

Notes in *italics* without a label are my own observations, usually from checking the raw Excel files by hand.

**What was given to the AI:** the handoff guide PDF, screenshots and text copies of R output, and descriptions of spreadsheet layouts. Personal names and coordinate values were left out of anything shared. The AI never had the raw files; all code ran on my computer.

**Sessions:** 5 Nov (evening), 6 Nov, 7 Nov 2026. Part of the 6 Nov work (exclusions, the start of the taxon audit) was done in a second chat and is logged in the same way.

**Requirements to render:** the raw Excel files in `AI_data/Data/Raw/` (kept locally only, not on GitHub) and the processed files in `AI_data/Data/Processed/`.

# Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(janitor)
library(tidyxl)

proc_dir <- here("AI_data", "Data", "Processed")
raw_dir  <- here("AI_data", "Data", "Raw")

opihi_master              <- read_csv(file.path(proc_dir, "opihi_master.csv"))
opihi_samples             <- read_csv(file.path(proc_dir, "opihi_samples.csv"))
opihi_surveys             <- read_csv(file.path(proc_dir, "opihi_surveys.csv"))
opihi_qc_flags            <- read_csv(file.path(proc_dir, "opihi_qc_flags.csv"))
opihi_exclusions_log      <- read_csv(file.path(proc_dir, "opihi_exclusions_log.csv"))
opihi_unmatched_names     <- read_csv(file.path(proc_dir, "opihi_unmatched_names.csv"))
opihi_data_dictionary     <- read_csv(file.path(proc_dir, "opihi_data_dictionary.csv"))
opihi_compiled_crosscheck <- read_csv(file.path(proc_dir, "opihi_compiled_crosscheck.csv"))
```

> **Me:** please just send me one step at a time so I don't get confused and we get lost again. Let's take it one by one.
>
> **Claude:** Agreed. One check per message, each with what to expect and how to read the output.

# Part 1 · Does every master value come from a raw cell? (5 Nov)

The question: did the AI copy every count correctly from the raw Excel files, or did it change or invent any values? The master's `source_cell` column records the raw file, tab, row and column each value came from, so each row can be looked up in the raw file.

## 1.1 Read the source location of each master row

```{r}
#| label: parse-source-cell
master_src <- opihi_master |>
  mutate(
    master_id = row_number(),
    src_file  = str_extract(source_cell, "(?i)^.*?\\.xls[xm]?"),
    src_sheet = str_match(source_cell, "\\|(.+)!R\\d+")[, 2],
    src_row   = as.integer(str_match(source_cell, ".*!R(\\d+)")[, 2]),
    src_col   = as.integer(str_match(source_cell, "C(\\d+)$")[, 2])
  )

# every row should have a file and a row number: expect 0 rows
master_src |> filter(is.na(src_file) | is.na(src_row)) |> count(source_family)
```

## 1.2 Read every raw cell with its true position

`tidyxl` keeps the real Excel row and column numbers (`readxl` can skip leading blank rows and shift them).

```{r}
#| label: raw-cells
raw_files <- list.files(raw_dir, pattern = "\\.xlsx$", full.names = TRUE, recursive = TRUE)
raw_files <- raw_files[!str_detect(basename(raw_files), "^~\\$")]   # skip Excel lock files

raw_cells <- map(raw_files, \(p) {
  xlsx_cells(p) |>
    filter(!is_blank) |>
    transmute(src_file = basename(p), sheet, row, col, data_type, numeric, character)
}) |> list_rbind()

# master files that don't exist in Raw: expect character(0)
setdiff(unique(master_src$src_file), unique(raw_cells$src_file))
```

> **Me:** When I ran `setdiff(...)` I got one xlsx file: "Copy of OPIHI Field Study 2025 - ALL Group Data (P1_P2) - use this one", but in the Raw folder the file is "... use this one!", so there is an exclamation mark missing between the two.
>
> **Claude:** The bug was in my parsing code, not the data. `source_cell` uses `!` to separate the file from the row, and my first regex stopped at the first `!`, cutting the file name short. Fixed by reading the file name up to `.xlsx` and the row from the last `!R` (the version above).

## 1.3 Families A and B (legacy and modern sheets)

Families A and B don't record the tab name in `source_cell`, so a row and column can exist on several tabs of one workbook. The check therefore requires the **taxon name** to sit in the same row or column as the value on that tab.

```{r}
#| label: ab-check
labels <- raw_cells |>
  filter(data_type == "character") |>
  transmute(src_file, sheet, row, col, label = str_squish(str_to_lower(character)))

row_labels <- labels |> distinct(src_file, sheet, row, label) |> mutate(label_in_row = TRUE)
col_labels <- labels |> distinct(src_file, sheet, col, label) |> mutate(label_in_col = TRUE)

ab2 <- master_src |>
  filter(source_family %in% c("A", "B")) |>
  mutate(taxon_key = str_squish(str_to_lower(taxon_raw))) |>
  left_join(raw_cells,
            by = c("src_file", "src_row" = "row", "src_col" = "col"),
            relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  left_join(row_labels, by = c("src_file", "sheet", "src_row" = "row", "taxon_key" = "label")) |>
  left_join(col_labels, by = c("src_file", "sheet", "src_col" = "col", "taxon_key" = "label")) |>
  mutate(
    label_ok = coalesce(label_in_row, FALSE) | coalesce(label_in_col, FALSE),
    value_ok = !is.na(numeric) & numeric == count,
    status = case_when(
      label_ok & value_ok                 ~ "1 match",
      label_ok & data_type %in% "numeric" ~ "2 value mismatch",
      label_ok                            ~ "3 raw cell not numeric",
      value_ok                            ~ "4 value matches, taxon label not found on that tab",
      TRUE                                ~ "5 no usable match"
    ))

# keep the best result for each master row
ab_best2 <- ab2 |> arrange(master_id, status) |> distinct(master_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

nrow(ab_best2)                            # expect 22,241 (all A + B rows)
ab_best2 |> count(source_family, status)  # expect only "1 match"
```

> **Claude (first attempt):** a plain join on file, row and column reported 370 "mismatches", and its row counts added up to more than the whole master (22,638 vs 22,588).
>
> **Claude (diagnosis):** a many-to-many join. Workbooks with several tabs returned one hit per tab, so a real match on one tab was paired with a non-match on another. Requiring the taxon label on the same tab fixed it.

**Result:** all 22,241 Family A and B rows are `1 match`. Every value was traced to a raw cell on a specific tab with the right taxon label, and the 370 earlier "mismatches" were false alarms caused by my join, not by the data.

**What this does not prove (Claude):** that nothing was lost (reverse check), that values sit in the right sample, that taxon cleaning was right, or anything about Family C. Those are the later parts.

## 1.4 Family C (classroom group files), forward check

For Family C the sample's column comes from `opihi_samples$sample_key`.

```{r}
#| label: c-forward
c_check <- master_src |>
  filter(source_family == "C") |>
  left_join(opihi_samples |> select(sample_id, sample_key), by = "sample_id") |>
  mutate(
    src_col   = as.integer(str_match(sample_key, "\\|c(\\d+)$")[, 2]),
    taxon_key = str_squish(str_to_lower(taxon_raw))
  ) |>
  left_join(raw_cells, by = c("src_file", "src_sheet" = "sheet", "src_row" = "row", "src_col" = "col")) |>
  left_join(row_labels, by = c("src_file", "src_sheet" = "sheet", "src_row" = "row", "taxon_key" = "label")) |>
  mutate(
    label_ok = coalesce(label_in_row, FALSE),
    value_ok = !is.na(numeric) & numeric == count,
    status = case_when(
      label_ok & value_ok                 ~ "match",
      label_ok & data_type %in% "numeric" ~ "value mismatch",
      label_ok                            ~ "raw cell not numeric",
      value_ok                            ~ "value matches, taxon label not in that row",
      TRUE                                ~ "no usable match"
    ))

nrow(c_check)          # expect 347
c_check |> count(status)
```

**Result:** 347 of 347 match. A + B + C = 22,241 + 347 = 22,588, the whole master.

## 1.5 Family C, reverse check: is any raw count missing from master?

```{r}
#| label: c-reverse
c_cols <- opihi_samples |>
  filter(survey_id %in% master_src$survey_id[master_src$source_family == "C"]) |>
  transmute(src_file  = str_extract(sample_key, "^[^|]+"),
            src_sheet = str_match(sample_key, "^[^|]+\\|([^|]+)\\|")[, 2],
            src_col   = as.integer(str_match(sample_key, "\\|c(\\d+)$")[, 2])) |>
  distinct()
anyNA(c_cols)    # expect FALSE

# data rows lie between the "Organism" and "TOTAL" labels, in column A or B
c_layout <- raw_cells |>
  semi_join(c_cols, by = c("src_file", "sheet" = "src_sheet")) |>
  filter(col %in% 1:2, data_type == "character") |>
  group_by(src_file, sheet) |>
  summarise(first_row = min(row[str_detect(character, regex("^organism", ignore_case = TRUE))]),
            last_row  = min(row[str_detect(character, regex("^total", ignore_case = TRUE))]),
            .groups = "drop")
c_layout    # expect no Inf

raw_c <- raw_cells |>
  inner_join(c_cols,   by = c("src_file", "sheet" = "src_sheet", "col" = "src_col")) |>
  inner_join(c_layout, by = c("src_file", "sheet")) |>
  filter(row > first_row, row < last_row, data_type == "numeric", numeric > 0)

in_master <- c_check |> distinct(src_file, src_sheet, src_row, src_col)

nrow(raw_c)    # expect 347
raw_c |> anti_join(in_master,
  by = c("src_file", "sheet" = "src_sheet", "row" = "src_row", "col" = "src_col")) |>
  select(src_file, sheet, row, col, numeric)    # raw counts missing from master: expect 0 rows

# numbers stored as text would escape the check above: expect 0
raw_cells |>
  inner_join(c_cols, by = c("src_file", "sheet" = "src_sheet", "col" = "src_col")) |>
  filter(data_type == "character", str_detect(character, "^\\s*[0-9.]+\\s*$")) |> nrow()
```

> **Claude (first attempt):** searched for the labels in column A only. The 2025 P1 tab came back as `Inf` (no label found) and the Waipuilani file was skipped, so only 202 raw counts were tested.
>
> **Me:** *(sent the label positions for both 2025 tabs)*
>
> **Claude:** P1 is shifted one column to the right and has three more rows; the data are fine. Searching columns A and B fixes it. (I also expected 283 instead of 347 because I forgot the Waipuilani file has the same layout.)

**Result:** 347 raw counts, all in master; 0 numbers stored as text. **Family C is verified in both directions.**

# Part 2 · Does the master agree with the sample table? (5 Nov)

```{r}
#| label: master-vs-samples
master_totals <- opihi_master |>
  group_by(sample_id) |>
  summarise(master_sum = sum(count), master_taxa = n(), .groups = "drop")

sample_mismatch <- opihi_samples |>
  left_join(master_totals, by = "sample_id") |>
  mutate(master_sum = replace_na(master_sum, 0), master_taxa = replace_na(master_taxa, 0)) |>
  filter(point_sum != master_sum | n_taxa != master_taxa)

nrow(sample_mismatch)                                  # 730 on first run
sample_mismatch |> count(sum_off = point_sum != master_sum)   # sums never differ
```

> **Claude:** 730 samples disagree, but every one has the same point total; only the taxon count differs, and only in the modern files. Likely a definition difference, not lost data.
>
> **Me:** *(sent the handoff guide PDF)*
>
> **Claude:** The data dictionary defines `n_taxa` as **non-substrate** taxa, while my check counted every row including Rock, sand and Rubble. Modern sheets record substrate, which is why only they disagree. Test it:

```{r}
#| label: n-taxa-definition
opihi_master |>
  group_by(sample_id) |>
  summarise(ns_clean    = n_distinct(taxon_clean[!category %in% "Substrate"]),
            ns_analysis = n_distinct(analysis_taxon[!category %in% "Substrate"]),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  inner_join(opihi_samples |> select(sample_id, n_taxa), by = "sample_id") |>
  summarise(clean_disagree = sum(ns_clean != n_taxa),          # expect 0
            analysis_disagree = sum(ns_analysis != n_taxa))     # > 0 is expected (genus level)
```

**Result:** point totals agree in all 7,216 samples, and taxon counts agree once substrate is excluded. No data problem; the dictionary's wording ("non-substrate taxa") is correct but easy to misread.

# Part 3 · Duplicate visits and surveys without a site (5 Nov)

```{r}
#| label: same-site-same-date
# any site and date that appears in more than one survey
opihi_surveys |>
  group_by(site_name, date) |>
  filter(n() > 1) |>
  arrange(site_name, date) |>
  select(survey_id, source_file, site_name, date, resolution, n_samples) |>
  print(n = Inf)

# does any raw file contribute nothing to master? (should be the Family D cross-check files)
setdiff(basename(raw_files), unique(master_src$src_file))
```

> **Claude:** The 28 Mauliola surveys all have different dates, so no visit was entered twice; the two 2026 files cover different visits (25 Jan and 20 Apr). Three same-site, same-day pairs come from the same file with very different totals, so they look like different school groups, not copies. The real finding is **S0251** (2023 group file) and **S0252** (2025 group file), which have no site or date: 283 master rows that can't be used for site or year comparisons.
>
> **Claude (after reading the guide):** correction to my framing: the guide lists these two under Known caveats, so they weren't hidden. The accurate point is that `opihi_unmatched_names` can't catch a missing site, because an empty site never shows up as an unmatched name.

## 3.1 Recover S0251's site and transects

*I found that every chart in the 2023 group file is titled "Diamond Head (Le'ahi)", although no cell holds the site. The group labels (P1G1 … P2G7) also give the transect number after the G.*

```{r}
#| label: recover-s0251
# Leahi's details, taken from the existing legacy surveys
site_info <- opihi_surveys |>
  filter(site_name == "Leahi") |>
  group_by(site_name, site_alias_english, island) |>
  summarise(latitude = median(latitude, na.rm = TRUE),
            longitude = median(longitude, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
nrow(site_info)   # expect 1

fill_s0251 <- function(df) {
  df |>
    mutate(
      site_recovered     = survey_id == "S0251",
      site_name          = if_else(site_recovered, site_info$site_name, site_name),
      site_alias_english = if_else(site_recovered, site_info$site_alias_english, site_alias_english),
      island             = if_else(site_recovered, site_info$island, island)
    )
}

fill_transect <- function(df) {
  df |>
    mutate(
      transect_inferred = survey_id == "S0251",
      transect = if_else(transect_inferred,
                         as.numeric(str_extract(group_label, "(?<=G)\\d+")),
                         transect)
    )
}

surveys_completed <- opihi_surveys |>
  fill_s0251() |>
  mutate(recovery_source = if_else(site_recovered,
         "chart title 'Diamond Head (Le'ahi)' on all tabs of the 2023 group file; not in any cell",
         NA_character_))

master_completed  <- opihi_master  |> fill_s0251() |> fill_transect()
samples_completed <- opihi_samples |> fill_transect()   # keeps samples consistent with master

# checks: only S0251's site and transect columns changed
anti_join(opihi_master, master_completed,
          by = setdiff(names(opihi_master), c("site_name", "site_alias_english", "island", "transect"))) |>
  nrow()                                                       # expect 0
master_completed |> count(site_recovered)                      # TRUE = 125
master_completed |> filter(is.na(site_name)) |> count(survey_id)   # only S0252
sum(master_completed$count) == sum(opihi_master$count)         # TRUE

# start the change log
change_log <- tibble(
  change = c("S0251: site recovered as Leahi (site_name, site_alias_english, island)",
             "S0251: transect filled from the group label (P#G# -> transect #)"),
  rows   = c(sum(master_completed$site_recovered), sum(master_completed$transect_inferred)),
  reason = c("chart titles in the 2023 group file name Diamond Head (Le'ahi); no cell holds the site",
             "group labels encode the transect; column left blank by the cleaning"))
```

S0252 (2025 group file) stays without a site: nothing in that file identifies one.

# Part 4 · QC flags (5–6 Nov)

```{r}
#| label: qc-overview
opihi_qc_flags |> count(level, flag, sort = TRUE) |> print(n = Inf)

# do flagged samples exist? expect 0
opihi_qc_flags |> filter(level == "sample") |>
  anti_join(opihi_samples, by = c("ref" = "sample_id")) |> nrow()
```

**Result:** 296 flags, all sample-level flags point to real samples. Four cells hold two flags joined by `;`, so tests must search inside the text.

## 4.1 Is `points_over_25` applied correctly?

```{r}
#| label: points-over-25
over_flagged <- opihi_qc_flags |>
  filter(level == "sample", str_detect(flag, "points_over_25")) |>
  distinct(ref)
over_data <- opihi_samples |> filter(point_sum > points_possible)

nrow(over_flagged); nrow(over_data)    # both 230
over_data |> anti_join(over_flagged, by = c("sample_id" = "ref")) |> nrow()   # missed flags: 0
over_flagged |> anti_join(over_data, by = c("ref" = "sample_id")) |> nrow()   # wrong flags: 0

# the guide says 174 over-25 quadrats in legacy files "and more in modern files":
# where do the 230 come from? (Family A should be 174)
over_data |>
  left_join(opihi_master |> distinct(sample_id, source_family), by = "sample_id") |>
  count(source_family, sample_type)
```

**Result:** the rule is exactly right: 230 over the limit, all flagged, none flagged wrongly. The split is 174 legacy quadrats (Family A) + 56 modern quadrats (Family B), which matches the guide’s 174 for legacy files.

## 4.2 Does the sample table's flag column agree with the flag file?

```{r}
#| label: flag-agreement
full_join(
  opihi_samples |> filter(!is.na(sample_flag)) |>
    separate_longer_delim(sample_flag, ";") |> count(flag = sample_flag),
  opihi_qc_flags |> filter(level == "sample") |>
    separate_longer_delim(flag, ";") |> count(flag),
  by = "flag", suffix = c("_samples", "_qcflags")) |>
  print(n = Inf)
```

**Result:** identical for all five sample flag types.

## 4.3 Survey-level flags

```{r}
#| label: survey-flags
survey_refs <- opihi_qc_flags |> filter(level == "survey") |> pull(ref)
sum(survey_refs %in% opihi_surveys$src_key)    # expect 57 of 57

opihi_qc_flags |>
  filter(level == "survey", flag != "placeholder_time_removed") |>
  arrange(flag) |>
  print(n = Inf, width = Inf)
```

> **Claude (first attempt):** joined survey flags on `survey_id` and got 57 unmatched. My mistake: survey flags use a text key (file\|date\|site), which matches `src_key`. All 57 point to real surveys.

Notes on the 12 smaller survey flags:

- `time_assumed_pm` (5): unlabelled times such as 01:05 read as afternoon, consistent with the low tide. Reasonable.
- `no_site_or_date_in_file` (2): the 2023 and 2025 classroom files. Expected.
- `no_metadata_match` (1): its detail ("matched … within 7 days") is identical to `metadata_date_mismatch`, so the flag name contradicts its own detail.
- `site_corrected_by_coordinates` (3): large jumps (180–363 km), investigated below.

## 4.4 The three site corrections

```{r}
#| label: site-corrected
opihi_qc_flags |>
  filter(level == "survey", flag == "site_corrected_by_coordinates") |>
  left_join(opihi_surveys, by = c("ref" = "src_key")) |>
  select(survey_id, source_file, date, site_name, island, n_samples, detail) |>
  print(width = Inf)
```

> **Claude:** Master filed all three by their coordinates. The "(0.00 km)" shows the coordinates sit exactly on a reference point, so they were copied from a site list, not measured. Either the label or the coordinates could be the slip. I suggest using the teacher as a tiebreaker, since a teacher usually surveys the same island.
>
> **Me:** we have no idea if the same teacher surveyed the same island year after year though?
>
> **Claude:** Fair point; test it before relying on it.

```{r}
#| label: teacher-islands
# how many islands does each teacher survey?
opihi_surveys |>
  filter(!is.na(teacher_id)) |>
  group_by(teacher_id) |>
  summarise(n_islands = n_distinct(island)) |>
  count(n_islands, name = "n_teachers")

flagged_ids <- c("S0143", "S0167", "S0210")
opihi_surveys |>
  filter(teacher_id %in% teacher_id[survey_id %in% flagged_ids]) |>
  count(teacher_id, island, site_name, sort = TRUE) |>
  print(n = Inf)
```

> **Claude:** 65 of 69 teachers survey one island, so the test is usable. S0143's teacher has only Hawaii surveys, which supports master. S0167 and S0210 belong to T043, which appears on five islands (probably a shared or placeholder ID), so the teacher can't decide those. Looking at neighbouring blocks in the 2019 file, I said master was probably **wrong** for both.
>
> **Me:** we are required to create one master list so prob option 1 \[fix master\]? lmk which xlsx files to open just to see if I can clarify anything as well.

*Checked each block in the raw files (location written in the block header and totals row, coordinates typed in the block):*

> **Me:** for 5/2/2019, location Kamaole in JC8 and JA55, with lat and long in JA9 and JA10. For 5/3/2019 location Maili in IY8 and IW55.
>
> **Me:** 1/20/2019 location Diamond Head/Leahi with lat and long.
>
> **Me:** \[2018 block\] −155 and 19 … says Onekahakaha.
>
> **Claude:** That overturns my neighbour argument. **Master is correct for all three** (S0143 Onekahakaha, S0167 Leahi, S0210 Kamaole Beach Park). The flags' "labelled as" site came from the **neighbouring block**: the legacy parser read the location of the block next door, and the coordinate rule then restored the right site. No data fix is needed, but the bug could misplace a survey silently if the coordinates are missing, so every legacy survey is checked in Part 9.

## 4.5 Placeholder times

```{r}
#| label: placeholder-times
pt <- opihi_qc_flags |>
  filter(level == "survey", flag == "placeholder_time_removed") |>
  left_join(opihi_surveys, by = c("ref" = "src_key"))

pt |> count(detail)                       # all "start 0.0 stop 0.0417" (00:00-01:00)
pt |> summarise(n = n(), start_blank = sum(is.na(start_time)), stop_blank = sum(is.na(stop_time)))
pt |> count(source_file, sort = TRUE)
```

**Result:** all 45 were the 00:00–01:00 template default (Excel stores 1:00 as 1/24 = 0.0417), and all 45 are now blank. 43 are in the 2004–2008 files.

> **Claude:** Then stash it, so the teammates' version comes in untouched.

``` bash
# (not run by Quarto; commands used in the Terminal)
git add "AI data/Scripts/Nordli_script.qmd"
git commit -m "Verification checks: Family C reverse check and qc_flags"
git stash push -m "local report and OPIHI.Rproj edits" -- "AI data/Scripts/opihi_report.qmd" "AI data/OPIHI/OPIHI.Rproj"
git pull --no-rebase --no-edit
git config pull.rebase false
```

The team had renamed the folder `AI data` to `AI_data`, which left an old copy holding untracked raw files.

> **Me:** well now there's two AI data folders.
>
> **Claude:** The old one only holds untracked leftovers. Compare the two raw folders before moving it.

*20 of 21 raw files were identical; the Waipuilani file differed.* The comparison (run once, old copy now in a Desktop backup):

```{r}
#| label: waipuilani-versions
#| eval: false
wp <- "OPIHI Field Study 2026 - Waipuilani Data.xlsx"
old_wp <- xlsx_cells(file.path("~/Desktop/opihi_backup/old_AI_data_folder/Data/Raw", wp))
new_wp <- xlsx_cells(file.path(raw_dir, wp))
keep <- c("sheet", "row", "col", "data_type", "numeric", "character")
bind_rows(
  only_new = anti_join(new_wp |> select(all_of(keep)), old_wp |> select(all_of(keep)), by = keep),
  only_old = anti_join(old_wp |> select(all_of(keep)), new_wp |> select(all_of(keep)), by = keep),
  .id = "where") |>
  count(where, sheet)
```

> **Me:** old file: B26 – Sargassum aquifolium / Sargassum polyphyllum; B31 – Pterocladiella capillacea / caerulescens … which looks like two species entries in each cell.
>
> **Claude:** The only changes are invisible line breaks (`\n` became `\r\n`) and recalculated proportion formulas, so no count or name changed and the Family C result holds. Separately, two cells list **two taxa in one cell**: master filed the *Sargassum* row as *Sargassum* spp.; the *Pterocladiella* row has no counts.

Paths in this script were then updated from `AI data` to `AI_data`.

> **Me:** I see that the raw folder is in the Rproj, which shouldn't go on GitHub. Help me remove. … just remove the entire raw folder from GitHub, no need to keep an empty folder there.

``` bash
git rm -r --cached "AI_data/Data/Raw"
printf '\nAI_data/Data/Raw/\n' >> .gitignore
git add .gitignore
git commit -m "Remove raw data folder from GitHub"
git push
```

`Raw/` is now local only and ignored by git (it remains in the commit history).

# Part 7 · Exclusions log (5–6 Nov)

```{r}
#| label: exclusions-overview
opihi_exclusions_log |> count(level, reason, sort = TRUE)     # 427 in total
```

## 7.1 The 107 Longitudinal `no_taxon_data` rows and the 6 invalid names

*Manual check of the 2026 Longitudinal file: column BF has no species header and a stray "3" where the name should be (the 6 `invalid_taxon_name` cells). Rows 97–266 are template rows with date or location only and no counts. The Mauliola transect and metadata rows have recorders, date and location but no organisms.*

> **Claude:** The six "3.0" exclusions are a data-entry problem in the sheet, not data loss. The 107 rows are an unfilled session (2026-01-25, S0247 has its 26 entered quadrats). A quadrat with a location but no organisms is "not recorded", not a true zero, which master can't represent.

## 7.2 The 309 blank template rows and the 2 other `no_taxon_data` rows

```{r}
#| label: blank-rows
bl <- opihi_exclusions_log |>
  filter(reason == "blank_template_row") |>
  mutate(src_file = source_file, row = as.integer(str_extract(source_ref, "(?<=\\|r)\\d+")))
anyNA(bl$row)    # expect FALSE

taxon_cols <- master_src |> filter(src_file %in% unique(bl$src_file)) |> distinct(src_file, src_col)
counts_tab <- raw_cells |>
  filter(str_detect(sheet, regex("pt\\s*counts", ignore_case = TRUE))) |>
  semi_join(taxon_cols, by = c("src_file", "col" = "src_col"))

bl |> inner_join(counts_tab, by = c("src_file", "row")) |>
  filter(data_type == "numeric", numeric > 0) |> nrow()     # counts on excluded rows: expect 0

two <- opihi_exclusions_log |>
  filter(reason == "no_taxon_data", !str_detect(source_file, "Longitudinal")) |>
  mutate(src_file = source_file, row = as.integer(str_extract(source_ref, "(?<=\\|r)\\d+")))
taxon_cols2 <- master_src |> filter(src_file %in% two$src_file) |> distinct(src_file, src_col)

raw_cells |>
  filter(str_detect(sheet, regex("pt\\s*counts", ignore_case = TRUE))) |>
  inner_join(two |> select(src_file, row), by = c("src_file", "row")) |>
  semi_join(taxon_cols2, by = c("src_file", "col" = "src_col")) |>
  count(src_file, data_type, has_count = coalesce(numeric, 0) > 0)   # expect no rows
```

> **Claude (first attempt):** my check of the two rows left out the counts-tab filter and reported a count, which was actually on the Metadata tab. Ignore it; the version above is the valid test.

**Result:** none of the 309 blank rows or the 2 stray rows has a count in a taxon column.

Blocks run newest (block01, March) to oldest (block07, January), so block08 is from January 2020 or earlier; even the year can't be assumed. # Part 8 · Taxon names (6–7 Nov)

```{r}
#| label: s0251-names
master_completed |>
  filter(survey_id == "S0251") |>
  distinct(taxon_raw, taxon_clean, analysis_taxon, category) |>
  arrange(taxon_clean) |>
  print(n = Inf, width = Inf)
```

> **Claude:** every misspelling in S0251 (e.g. Turbinania, Caiclmus, Byropsis) maps to the right species. `opihi_unmatched_names` is empty because the crosswalk was built from the same data it was applied to, so it can only catch new spellings. Two mappings look wrong: "unknown Fish" is categorised as Invertebrate, and *Dendropoma gregarium* became "gregaria".

```{r}
#| label: fish-dendropoma
master_completed |>
  filter(str_detect(taxon_clean, regex("fish|gregari", ignore_case = TRUE))) |>
  count(taxon_raw, taxon_clean, category, name = "n_rows")
```

> **Me:** fish is a vertebrate for sure.
>
> **Claude:** 172 rows were already spelled *gregaria* in the sheets, so the AI picked the majority spelling; all three spellings correctly end up as one taxon. Only the label is in question.
>
> **Me:** use gregarium instead and add vertebrate.

```{r}
#| label: fix-names
n_before <- nrow(master_completed)

master_completed <- master_completed |>
  mutate(
    across(c(taxon_clean, analysis_taxon),
           ~ if_else(.x == "Dendropoma gregaria", "Dendropoma gregarium", .x)),
    category = if_else(coalesce(taxon_clean == "Unknown fish", FALSE), "Vertebrate", category))

nrow(master_completed) == n_before    # TRUE
master_completed |>
  filter(str_detect(taxon_clean, regex("fish|gregari", ignore_case = TRUE))) |>
  count(taxon_raw, taxon_clean, analysis_taxon, category, name = "n_rows")

change_log <- change_log |>
  add_row(change = "taxon 'Dendropoma gregaria' -> 'Dendropoma gregarium'",
          rows = sum(master_completed$taxon_clean == "Dendropoma gregarium", na.rm = TRUE),
          reason = "accepted spelling; the AI used the majority raw spelling") |>
  add_row(change = "category of 'Unknown fish': Invertebrate -> Vertebrate", rows = 1,
          reason = "fish are vertebrates; the category list had no vertebrate option")
```

## 8.1 One taxon per sample

```{r}
#| label: duplicates
dups <- master_completed |>
  count(sample_id, taxon_clean, name = "n_rows") |>
  filter(n_rows > 1)
dups    # 2: Sargassum aquifolium and Turbinaria ornata, both in S0251-003

master_completed |>
  semi_join(dups, by = c("sample_id", "taxon_clean")) |>
  select(sample_id, taxon_raw, taxon_clean, count, source_cell)
```

> **Claude:** in each pair a misspelling and the correct name were on separate sheet lines; the crosswalk fixed the typo and they collapsed onto one name. Recommend summing them.
>
> **Me:** the Excel sheet has two rows with observations for Turbinaria, just with different spelling.

```{r}
#| label: merge-duplicates
cols_before  <- names(master_completed)
total_before <- sum(master_completed$count, na.rm = TRUE)
dup_keys     <- dups |> select(sample_id, taxon_clean)

merged <- master_completed |>
  semi_join(dup_keys, by = c("sample_id", "taxon_clean")) |>
  group_by(across(-c(taxon_raw, count, source_cell))) |>
  summarise(taxon_raw   = paste(taxon_raw, collapse = "; "),
            source_cell = paste(source_cell, collapse = "; "),
            count       = sum(count), .groups = "drop")
nrow(merged)    # expect 2

master_completed <- master_completed |>
  anti_join(dup_keys, by = c("sample_id", "taxon_clean")) |>
  bind_rows(merged) |>
  select(all_of(cols_before))

nrow(master_completed)                                      # 22,586
sum(master_completed$count, na.rm = TRUE) == total_before   # TRUE
master_completed |> count(sample_id, taxon_clean) |> filter(n > 1) |> nrow()   # 0

change_log <- change_log |> add_row(
  change = "merged duplicate taxon rows in S0251-003 (Sargassum aquifolium 1+2 = 3, Turbinaria ornata 1+1 = 2)",
  rows = 2,
  reason = "typo and correct spelling entered on separate sheet lines (confirmed in raw file); counts summed, both source cells kept")
```

> **Claude (first attempt):** the merge grouped by every other column and returned 4 rows, so nothing merged. The pairs also differ in `source_cell`; combining that column too (above) fixed it.
>
> **Me:** the Excel sheet shows total Turbinaria from the two entries are 4 and 22 though? … for P1 … and 6 for 2025 P1.
>
> **Claude:** The sheet's total adds up all groups; master stores each group as its own sample. Check the totals per spelling:

```{r}
#| label: turbinaria-totals
master_src |>
  filter(taxon_clean == "Turbinaria ornata", str_detect(src_sheet, "P1")) |>
  group_by(src_file, src_sheet, survey_id, taxon_raw) |>
  summarise(n_samples = n(), total = sum(count), .groups = "drop")
```

**Result:** 2023 P1 = 4 (Turbinania) + 22 (Turbinaria) and 2025 P1 = 6, matching the sheet totals. Master has every count; the merge only joins the two lines within S0251-003.

## 9.1 Is every legacy survey filed under the site written in its own block?

This tests whether the neighbouring-block bug from Part 4.4 misplaced any survey. A block's location is written at its first data column (totals row) and two columns to the right (header), so a block owns every column from its first data column up to the start of the next block. I calibrated this on S0210 and S0211, whose cells I had checked by hand.

```{r}
#| label: block-location-check
# site names and the text that identifies them in the raw sheets
# ('okina and apostrophes are removed before matching)
site_lookup <- tribble(~site_name, ~pattern,
  "Hilo Yacht Club","hilo yacht", "Holoholokai","holoholokai", "Kahaluu Bay","kahaluu",
  "Kaupo","kaupo", "Keei","keei", "Keiki Ponds","keiki pond", "Kiholo Bay","kiholo",
  "Kona Bay Estates","kona bay", "Old Airport","old airport", "Onekahakaha","onekahakaha",
  "Oneo Bay","oneo", "Punaluu Beach Park","punaluu", "Richardsons","richardson",
  "Waiopae","waiopae", "Wawaloli","wawaloli", "Fuji","fuji", "Mahaulepu","mahaulepu",
  "Nukolii","nukolii", "Salt Pond","salt pond", "Waipouli","waipouli", "Hulopoe Bay","hulopoe",
  "Kamaole Beach Park","kamaole", "Keawakapu","keawakapu", "Napili Bay","napili",
  "Waipuilani","waipuilani", "Kapukahehu","kapukahehu", "Mapulehu","mapulehu",
  "Moomomi","moomomi", "Morris Point","morris", "Baby Makapuu","makapuu",
  "Ewa","\\bewa\\b", "Kahana Bay","kahana", "Kalaeloa","kalaeloa|barbers? ?point",
  "Keiki Bay","keiki bay", "Lanikai Point","lanikai", "Leahi","leahi|diamond head",
  "Maili Beach","maili", "Mauliola","mauliola|sand island", "Mokauea Island","mokauea",
  "Sandy Beach","sandy", "Turtle Bay","turtle bay", "Waianae High School Reef","waianae")

legacy <- surveys_completed |>
  filter(str_detect(src_key, "\\|block")) |>
  select(survey_id, source_file, date, site_name)

spans <- master_src |>
  semi_join(legacy, by = "survey_id") |>
  group_by(survey_id, src_file) |>
  summarise(min_col = min(src_col), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(src_file) |> arrange(min_col, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  mutate(end_col = lead(as.numeric(min_col), default = Inf) - 1) |> ungroup()

# legacy files with more than one tab would need extra care: expect 0 rows
raw_cells |> filter(src_file %in% spans$src_file) |>
  distinct(src_file, sheet) |> count(src_file) |> filter(n > 1)

site_cells <- raw_cells |>
  filter(src_file %in% spans$src_file, data_type == "character") |>
  mutate(txt = tolower(character) |> str_remove_all("['ʻ‘’`]"))

site_hits <- map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(site_lookup)), \(i)
  site_cells |> filter(str_detect(txt, site_lookup$pattern[i])) |>
    transmute(src_file, row, col, label_site = site_lookup$site_name[i]))

own <- site_hits |>
  inner_join(spans, by = "src_file", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  filter(col >= min_col, col <= end_col) |>
  group_by(survey_id) |>
  summarise(labels = paste(sort(unique(label_site)), collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop")

block_check <- legacy |>
  left_join(own, by = "survey_id") |>
  mutate(status = case_when(
    is.na(labels) ~ "no label found",
    map2_lgl(site_name, coalesce(labels, ""), \(s, l) s %in% str_split_1(l, ", ")) ~ "match",
    TRUE ~ "different"))

block_check |> count(status)    # expect 227 match
block_check |> filter(status != "match")
```

> **Claude (first attempt):** 189 match, 0 different, 38 "no label found", all at Mauliola, Kalaeloa or Hulopoe Bay. These blocks use other names (Sand Island, Barbers Point) or the ʻokina (Hulopoʻe). Adding those (above) gave the final result. Two smaller coding errors on the way (a number-type clash in `lead()` and `case_when()` evaluating `NA` labels) were also mine.

**Result:** all 227 legacy surveys are filed under the site written in their own block. The parser bug only changed the wording of the three flags; it never placed a survey at the wrong site.

| Area | Result |

| Families A and B vs raw cells | 22,241 of 22,241 match |

| QC flags | All 296 resolve; `points_over_25` exactly right (230); placeholder times correct (45) |
| Site corrections (3) | Master correct; flag wording came from the neighboring block |
| All legacy site labels | 227 of 227 match their own block |
| Compiled cross-check | 234 found; 18 confirmed empty |
| Exclusions (427) | All accounted for; block08 is the one real data loss |

**Open items:** my keep/fix/exclude rule for each flag type.

## Where the AI was wrong, and how it was caught

| \# | AI error | How it was caught | Fix |
|----|----|----|----|
| 1 | Regex cut file names at the first `!` | I noticed the missing "!" in the file name | Read up to `.xlsx` |
| 2 | Many-to-many join gave 370 false mismatches | Row counts exceeded the master | Require the taxon label on the same tab |
| 3 | Reverse check looked only in column A | `Inf` in `c_layout` | Search columns A and B |
| 4 | Expected 283 instead of 347 rows | Output | Forgot the Waipuilani file |
| 5 | Stray-row check missed the tab filter | Hit was on the Metadata tab | Added the counts-tab filter |
| 6 | Joined survey flags on the wrong key | 57 unmatched | Use `src_key` |
| 7 | Assumed teachers stay on one island | I questioned it | Tested first (65 of 69) |
| 8 | Concluded master was wrong for S0167/S0210 from neighbouring blocks | My check of the raw blocks | Master was right; flag text was wrong |
| 9 | Merge grouped by `source_cell` and merged nothing | `nrow(merged)` = 4 | Combine `source_cell` too |
| 10 | Site patterns missed English names and the ʻokina | 38 "no label found" | Added aliases, removed ʻokina |
| 11 | Two coding errors (`lead()` type, `case_when()` with `NA`) | R errors | Fixed in the code |
